issues.body: The FLOW_WORDS rejection checks only `entry[0][0]`, the first token of each `;`/`&`-delimited list. It never checks commands produced later by `split_on(list_tokens, "&&")`. For example, with PyYAML genuinely proven in another RUN, `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version` is accepted: the list is eligible because it starts with `true`, splitting records `["jq", "--version"]`, but the shell exits successfully before jq and the image build remains green. `exec true` in the same position provides an equivalent bypass. The added `exit` fixture only exercises a flow word at the start of a list, so it does not catch this realistic mutation of the claimed reachability guarantee.
issues.fix_hint: Reject a RUN when any command position that can transfer control is encountered, including commands after `&&`, before recording probes from it. Add a fixture with the other dependency genuinely proven and `RUN true && exit 0 && jq --version` (and preferably the analogous `exec true` form), asserting rejection and that jq is named.
issues.title: Control transfer after && still makes an unreachable probe count as proof

verdict.summary:
> 🤖 SPARQ agent

The round-2 examples are now rejected, but the reachability model still accepts probes after a control-transfer word when that word is not the first command in its semicolon-delimited list. A successful `exit` or `exec` can therefore terminate the shell before the accepted probe while leaving the RUN green. This preserves the same major proof-vs-presence defect, so progress is stagnant.
